## Introduction 

There are many ways to create data visualizations in R. The base R graphics system provides built-in plotting functions that are useful for quickly exploring data, and other visualization packages offer their own approaches and specialized features. In this course, however, we will focus on the `{ggplot2}` package.

`{ggplot2}` has become the most widely used data visualization package in the R ecosystem because of its flexibility, consistency, and extensibility. Built on the principles of the Grammar of Graphics, `{ggplot2}` allows users to create everything from simple scatterplots and bar charts to complex, publication-quality visualizations using a coherent and intuitive syntax. Its layered approach makes it easy to customize plots, add annotations, and incorporate additional data elements as needed.

Another advantage of `{ggplot2}` is its extensive ecosystem. Numerous extension packages build on `{ggplot2}`, providing specialized themes, color palettes, interactive graphics, and advanced visualization capabilities. Because it is so widely adopted in academia, industry, and data science workflows, learning `{ggplot2}` will equip you with skills that transfer across many projects and professional settings.

Our first data visualization using `{ggplot2}` will be the histogram.
